A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImmerIris work, and all 11 pages of v1 and 10 pages of v2 are readable. Neither contains the referenced supplementary material or appendices. In particular, v2 defers identification results there, preventing verification of their claimed relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, verification and identification experiments, and ablations in Figures 4–5 and Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original dataset analyses and retains verification, identification, and ablation results in Figure 5 and Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: IR-BBox becomes NormFree and IR-Norm becomes NormKeep. The proposed procedure retains square iris cropping, 1.2-fold bounding-box expansion, a ResNet backbone, and ArcFace training. Shortened implementation descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CASIA-IrisV4-Thousand and ImmerIris using verification and identification, single-eye and dual-eye modes, and the same eight challenge scenarios. Immer-Angle is renamed Immer-Gaze. Added demographic and motion-blur annotations do not establish new population or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Gabor, OM, Maxout, Maxout-BA, UE-UGCL, CM, ComplexIrisNet, and the normalization-retaining ablation. Renaming IR-Norm to NormKeep does not introduce a comparator. The alternative-normalization experiment receives a more specific attribution, without establishing a different evaluated method.

E3.justification: The overall evaluation design remains, but Sections 3.2–3.5 revise reported settings: training/test counts change from 347,297/154,184 to 347,927/151,864; quality assessment adds motion blur; Immer-Select reverses its eye-specific excluded gaze columns; and the stated impostor-pair cap becomes 3M throughout instead of 2M for isolated-factor protocols. These are reported protocol revisions, not evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands the quality-distribution analysis from five to six dimensions, adding motion blur and associated examples. It removes v1 Figure 4(b)'s per-subject sample-count distribution and accompanying imbalance discussion. The isolated-challenge analyses and backbone/normalization ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores. The quality-distribution plots are dataset descriptions, not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All shared experimental table scores are identical after matching renamed methods and protocols. However, degraded-image prevalence changes from approximately 46% to 42%, and Table 1 revises dataset counts, including VISOB from 75,428 to 95,107 images. Figure 2 also changes numerical content: the proposed Immer-Control point moves from 1−FRR approximately 0.85 to FRR approximately 5%, matching the retained 4.93% right-eye result. Right-eye and dual-eye identification rows are deferred to unavailable supplementary material, so their continued reporting cannot be verified.

T1.justification: Neither PDF presents formal theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The revision retains conceptual explanations of normalization and feature extraction without adding or revising formal theory.

C1.justification: The dataset, benchmark, and normalization-free contributions remain. v2 qualifies the method's superiority as occurring in 'most cases', whereas v1 repeatedly claims consistent outperformance. Dataset novelty is also reframed from early off-axis acquisition to early immersive applications.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's specific explanation that dilation mainly changes the unwrapped texture's aspect ratio and recasts the Light findings around sensitivity to illumination. It also replaces the favorable interpretation of IR-Norm's inherited face-recognition framework with emphasis on NormKeep trailing stronger baselines. The limitation under gaze variation remains.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Asian participants, the three lowest/highest brightness levels for Immer-Light, and a cited source for alternative normalization. Conversely, it omits the explicit CASIA 700/300-subject split, central-gaze gallery requirement, zero-padding rule, 64×512 normalization resolution, and TFace repository link. The IR-50 backbone, 112×112 input, SGD, and 32 epochs remain documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references on off-angle gaze, pupil dilation, biomechanical normalization, ArcFace, DuetFace, and biometric standards. It makes the on-axis/off-axis distinction in prior datasets more explicit. These additions strengthen support for the existing positioning without changing the central relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, dataset description, method explanation, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Dataset-related work now precedes recognition methods, controlled and cross-domain evaluations are merged, and method/protocol terminology is systematically revised.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redraws the scenario and method diagrams, redesigns Figure 2, replaces the sample-count histogram, and combines quality distributions with examples. It adds the protocol-factor matrix in Table 2 and an acquisition-axis column in Table 1, restyles result tables, and reduces the displayed identification table to left-eye results.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting through clearer organization, an explicit protocol matrix, split counts that now sum to 499,791, and corrected immersive curves in Figure 2 that agree with retained table values. These are useful but limited gains because the method and shared benchmark scores remain unchanged. Some reproducibility details disappear, and identification results are deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs, tempering the improvement.
